articles.title: Lamar Jackson house: Inside Ravens QB’s $900K, 8,000 sq ft Maryland mansion built in 1996 with a three car garage, home gym, and private pool
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson’s team, the Baltimore Ravens, won over the Dallas Cowboys by three points in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body: Lamar Jackson’s team, the Baltimore Ravens, won over the Dallas Cowboys by three points in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season.The 29-year-old quarterback threw for 185 yards and two touchdowns, and added 50 rushing yards on six carries. He has won two games and lost one so far this season.Aside from knowing he comes from a difficult childhood and owns a soul food restaurant in Pompano Beach, little is known about the signal-caller, especially where he lives.The year Jackson was drafted into the NFL was also the year he paid a discounted $900K in cash for an eight-bedroom home through his mother, Felicia Jones’ Florida-based LLC, according to the New York Post.While he was still a rookie, he told ESPN that the house was his first major purchase with his NFL money.He had signed a four-year, $9 million rookie contract with Baltimore in 2018. Let’s learn more about the mansion now.Lamar Jackson’s Maryland mansionAs per Velvet Ropes, the Maryland mansion was built in 1996 on a 3.3-acre plot. A local flipper added about $150K in upgrades before the house went up for sale in 2018.Lamar Jackson bought the property in 2018 through his mother Felicia Jones’ limited liability company, paying in cash rather than financing the purchase.According to Virtual Globetrotting, the house was purchased through Kokomo and Jut LLC, based in Florida.Jackson has shared the house with his mother and brother, Jamar Jackson, ever since. He lost his father and grandmother on the same day in 2005, when he was just 8 years old.This changed his household’s dynamics. His life became harder to get by. It taught him the importance of family and money.Lamar signed a massive $260 million contract with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, but he still lives in the Maryland home he bought as a rookie NFL player.The Baltimore Ravens also keep their practice facility in Owings Mills. The facility is just 20 minutes away from Jackson’s mansion.The 7,995 sq-ft mansion features eight bedrooms and seven bathrooms. It was sold for $900,000 in 2018, and Velvet Ropes estimates its value at $1.4 million.According to Omni Home Ideas, the Baltimore Ravens QB’s mansion is valued between $2 million to $5 million.Lamar Jackson’s home exterior design and architectureAccording to Omni Home Ideas, Lamar Jackson’s Owings Mills mansion blends sleek design with comfortable living.It features clean lines, expansive windows, and a strong focus on open spaces. The design reflects Jackson’s dynamic, innovative personality.Lamar Jackson’s house sits on a sprawling lot. It provides ample space for indoor and outdoor activities. It offers multiple bedrooms and bathrooms, plus grand entertaining spaces.The manicured, landscaped driveway leads to a striking entrance that speaks volumes about elegance and stature.A glimpse at the Ravens QB’s lavish interiorsThe main living room acts as a grand centerpiece with high ceilings and expansive windows. The space feels airy and open.The minimalist layout is defined by plush sofas and a few curated modern furniture pieces.Comfort takes priority, but modernity doesn’t disappear, thanks to luxe materials like velvet upholstery, polished wood coffee tables, and stone fireplaces.The kitchen feels like a culinary masterpiece, with state-of-the-art modern appliances, from top-of-the-line stainless steel ranges to a smart refrigerator that syncs with Ravens QB Lamar Jackson’s phone.The master bedroom suite features floor-to-ceiling windows, a private terrace, and a fireplace.The bathroom features a jacuzzi tub, a large rain shower, his-and-hers sinks, high-end marble floors, custom tiling, and sleek chrome fixtures.A dedicated study, home gym, and three car garageA private study area features built-in shelves, comfortable seating, and a desk with a view of the property.The Ravens QB’s home also boasts a state-of-the-art in-house gym with fully equipped cardio machines, free weights, and training gear.The gym has large windows that let in natural light. Recovery spaces like hot tubs and saunas add to the athletic lifestyle.According to the New York Post, the brick home with nine-foot ceilings has a curved staircase, a two-story foyer, wood floors, huge windows, and crown moldings.The mansion offers all the luxurious touches, including a recreation room, a gym, a whirlpool hot tub, a private pool and spa, a wet bar, two fireplaces, a breakfast nook, an office, a large patio, and a three-car garage.The three-car garage could be for Lamar’s, his mother Felicia Jones’, and his brother Jamar’s cars.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inside the ugly DMs with death threats, harassment and bullying that Cam Ward's sister received from Titans fans
articles.summary: Cam Ward’s difficult afternoon against the Giants did not end when the final whistle sounded.
articles.body: Cam Ward’s difficult afternoon against the Giants did not end when the final whistle sounded. The Tennessee Titans suffered a 12-7 loss at MetLife Stadium yesterday. Ward’s sister, Chantel, took to social media to address what she described as a wave of harassment directed at her and other members of their family.Chantel said people had been entering her direct messages on Facebook, X and Instagram following Titans games and sending what she characterized as threats, hate, bullying, personal attacks, and disrespect. Her message came shortly after Ward threw a costly interception in the final seconds of Tennessee's latest loss.Cam Ward’s sister: “The fact I even have to post this is diabolical”Chantel began her statement by expressing frustration that she felt the situation had become serious enough to address publicly.“The fact I even have to post this is diabolical,”she wrote in an Instagram Story, according to reports.She explained that fans see everything that happens during an NFL game, whether it’s a touchdown, interceptions, wins, losses, or press conferences, but don't necessarily see what happens to the people closest to players once the game is over.According to Chantel, that has meant people taking their frustration with Cam directly to her social-media accounts.She said the messages included “threats, hate, bullying, personal attacks and disrespect”toward her and her family.Chantel also claimed that the screenshots she had shared publicly represented only a fraction of the messages she had received.Chantel made it clear that she understands criticism comes with being an NFL quarterback.She said fans are entitled to criticize a player's performance and decisions on the field. But she drew a line between football criticism and personally targeting a player's relatives. Her argument was that Cam Ward is a quarterback to the fans watching on Sundays, but he is her younger brother away from the football field.That distinction formed the heart of her message.Chantel said she has “loved, protected, supported” Cam and watched him work toward his football career throughout his life. She argued that threats and harassment directed at a player's family should not be treated as simply another part of being a professional athlete.Cam Ward’s final throw sent Titans fans into frustrationChantel's statement came after one of the most painful endings possible for Tennessee. The Titans trailed the Giants for most of the afternoon but managed to put together a late comeback attempt. Ward helped Tennessee cut the deficit to five points with a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson. The Titans then got the ball back and drove deep into Giants territory, setting up a chance to potentially win the game. But the comeback ended at the worst possible moment.With Tennessee inside the Giants' 10-yard line, Ward rolled to his left and had an opportunity to run or potentially use one of the Titans' remaining timeouts. Instead, he attempted to throw toward the end zone.Giants safety Jevon Holland jumped the pass and intercepted it, sealing New York's 12-7 victory. The Titans officially finished the game 0-for-3 in the red zone. Ward finished the game 23-of-36 for 181 yards, one touchdown and one interception.The quarterback later acknowledged that he would have liked to make a better throw.“At the end of the day, if I throw it higher, it’s a different outcome,” Ward said after the game. He added that he did not believe the decision was reckless but acknowledged that it simply wasn't a good throw.Titans coach Robert Saleh also addressed the interceptionWard's final decision also drew criticism from Titans head coach Robert Saleh. Saleh pointed out that Ward had room to run and said the quarterback needed to be more careful with the football in that situation.“We’ve got two timeouts left, it’s first and goal,”Saleh said. “We’re gonna score, you don’t need to force it in that situation.”That criticism is separate from the online harassment Chantel described. While coaches and fans can evaluate Ward's performance, Chantel's complaint was specifically about people allegedly taking that frustration into her personal messages and directing it toward his family.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brittany Mahomes' iconic tattoo goes viral: eagle-eyed fans spot the adorable detail
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes gave fans another glimpse into her life as a mom as she shared a sweet family moment from the football stands, and her sentimental
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes gave fans another glimpse into her life as a mom as she shared a sweet family moment from the football stands, and her sentimental tattoos quietly caught fans' attention. In a photo shared on Instagram, Brittany was seen enjoying a game with her children, with daughter Golden Raye Mahomes sitting happily in front of her. The adorable family moment also offered a closer look at the tattoos Brittany has dedicated to the people and pets closest to her.Brittany Mahomes’ meaningful tattoos tell the story of her growing familyBrittany's collection of tattoos isn't simply about body art. Several of her designs hold deeply personal meanings connected to her family. Her wrist tattoo features Sterling's name written in cursive, with her birthday underneath. She also has Bronze's name and birthday incorporated into the design. Golden's addition to the family brought another sentimental detail to Brittany's ink.According to a description of the tattoos, Golden's name and birthday are connected to a twisted line that appears to form a flower, giving the design an especially delicate touch. The designs mean that Brittany carries a small reminder of each of her children with her wherever she goes.A tribute to Sterling, Bronze and GoldenBrittany and Patrick welcomed their first child, Sterling Skye, in February 2021. Their son, Patrick “Bronze” Lavon Mahomes III, followed in November 2022, before the couple welcomed their third child, Golden Raye, in January 2025.Brittany has previously spoken about the thought behind the names Sterling and Bronze. In an Instagram Q&A, she explained that she originally considered the name Sterling for one of the family's dogs because it went well with their dog Steel. She eventually decided that Sterling was meant to be her daughter's name instead, while Silver became the name of their second dog. The family's names therefore have a connection that stretches beyond Brittany and Patrick's children.Her dogs also have a place in her tattoo collectionBrittany's children aren't the only members of the family represented in her ink. On her other wrist, she has a paw-print tattoo dedicated to her two dogs, Steel and Silver.The detail adds another sweet layer to Brittany's tattoo collection, especially considering the connection between the names of her dogs and her children's names. What began with Steel and Silver eventually became part of the naming story surrounding Sterling as well.In the latest Instagram post, however, it was Golden who immediately captured attention. The little girl was pictured smiling from the family's suite, dressed in a red-and-white outfit while the football field could be seen behind her.Brittany captioned the post, “Three and zerooooooo 🙏❤️,” celebrating the team's record. The post quickly attracted attention from family, friends and fans, with Patrick himself leaving a series of red-heart emojis in the comments.Brittany has previously shown off her meaningful inkThis isn't the first time Brittany has given fans a glimpse at the tattoos celebrating her family. In 2023, she showed off tattoos featuring Sterling and Bronze's names and birthdates on her wrist. At the time, Brittany revealed that she had four tattoos in total. The collection has since grown alongside her family, with Golden's arrival bringing another meaningful design.Earlier this year, Brittany also debuted a tattoo tribute to all three of her children, with a design featuring the outlines of their faces. From their children's names and birthdays to a paw print for their beloved dogs, Brittany's tattoos tell a story about the people who mean the most to her.And while the latest Instagram post was primarily about celebrating a football victory, the glimpse of her sentimental ink added another wholesome detail to the family moment.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Did the Chiefs' TE Travis Kelce really touch down shirtless ahead of the game against the Miami Dolphins?
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, is navigating through a pretty strong season in the league amid all the buzz around his personal life and
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, is navigating through a pretty strong season in the league amid all the buzz around his personal life and high profile marriage. While Travis Kelce’s team, the Kansas City Chiefs, secured a third consecutive win in Week 3 against the Miami Dolphins, there have been rumors about him allegedly arriving shirtless in Miami.Did Travis Kelce really walk shirtless ahead of the game against the Miami Dolphins?No, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, Travis Kelce did not arrive at the stadium shirtless to take the field against the Miami Dolphins.The popular tight end was spotted in a custom Tom Ford Kelly Green suit. Travis Kelce also wore a black T-shirt underneath his green suit and accessorized his look with a single silver chain and brown gradient sunglasses.In the last few hours, a fan page on X posted an AI generated image of Travis Kelce walking shirtless as the team had touched down in Miami.Though the post is completely fake, it has convinced many fans. The post of the caption read as, “Travis Kelce spotted shirtless with a green pants while touching down in Miami”.A fan took to X and wrote, “Damn, he must’ve shaved a lot! 😬 Every time I’ve seen a pic when no shirt he’s covered in hair.”Another fan posted, “the way he looks like hes just landing from a whole other tax bracket and still chose the olive green pants is sending me.”A third fan wrote, “Because he knew somebody would take a photo and post it. At least he’s performing good somewhere. Is Taylor in the kitchen? He might be the Delilah to her Samson career.”Another fan posted, “the bus saying academy is sending me cause that man is built like a school project gone right”.A fifth fan noted, “He’s a hairy man. Why do you think his nickname is “Big Yeti”. I’m afraid this is a big fat lie.”However, neither Travis Kelce nor the Kansas City Chiefs has responded to the fake rumors yet as he remains focused on his career.Travis Kelce remains unbeatable in the new seasonTravis Kelce had a record breaking start to the 2026 NFL season for the Kansas City Chiefs. In Week 1, he caught 3 passes for 71 yards as he claimed the second spot on NFL's all-time tight end receiving yards list.The popular tight end dominated Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts with 9 catches for 101 yards and a touchdown, while also setting the NFL career record for yards after the catch.In Week 3, as he faced the Miami Dolphins, Travis Kelce recorded 59 yards and a touchdown.In an interview, Patrick Mahomes opened up about Travis Kelce’s performance in Week 3 as he said, "Travis making the play. He caught the first pass and the last pass…Battling through when his number was called."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady reportedly struggled to see ex wife Gisele Bündchen move on as cryptic “True Love” post resurfaces
articles.summary: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, ended his marriage with Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bundchen in 2022 and has remained single ever
articles.body: Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, ended his marriage with Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bundchen in 2022 and has remained single ever since.While Gisele Bundchen has moved on,remarried and welcomed her third child with her new husband, it seems the series of events had left the NFL legend pretty hurt.Tom Brady could have expressed his anger over Gisele Bundchen moving on in her life with a new baby and a new husbandLars Anderson’s new biography about the former New England Patriots quarterback, titled Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness has sparked new speculations about his feelings,As per Daily Mail, in an excerpt from the biography, it states how the New England Patriots’ legend felt when he learned Gisele Bundchen gave birth to her third child in 2025.The excerpt from the biography read as, “Just over a month after the birth, Brady shared a photo of himself on Instagram — his preferred form of mass (and often cryptic) communication…”The excerpt added, “In the color photograph, Brady’s right arm is extended and a ball has spiraled out of his hand, silhouetted by the sunset’s golden glow. Underneath, Brady wrote: ‘True Love.’”Concerning the post Tom Brady made on his social media account, Lars Anderson wrote, “To those who knew him well, there was no ambiguity…As one friend described it, that was ‘the softest middle finger.’”For now, the speculations remain unconfirmed as neither Tom Brady nor his ex wife, former Victoria’s Secret supermodel Gisele Bundchen has responded to the claims about their lives yet.Tom Brady’s divorce with Gisele Bundchen continues to be in the news even after yearsTom Brady’s 13 year long marriage to Gisele Bundchen seemed pretty messy in the few years prior to their high profile divorce.The New England Patriots’ legend kept retiring and then coming back on the field which has sparked more speculations about how his focus on his career interfered with the life he had built with his ex wife and children.There were also many speculations about how Gisele Bundchen wanted Tom Brady to focus more on the life they share at home.However, there are no confirmations. In many of her interviews, the Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bundchen has said that things are not so “black and white” and she is proud of Tom Brady’s achievements on the field.The seven time Super Bowl champion and the New England Patriots’ legend has actually never spoken about his marriage ending in any interview.In the last few years, Tom Brady has remained focused on the career he has built as an athlete and an analyst as he stayed supportive and spends time with his three children.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "It was a little bit different": Jason Kelce reveals the truth about his changing relationship with Travis Kelce
articles.summary: Last year, Jason Kelce offered a rare look at how fame, family and the success of the “New Heights” podcast have reshaped his bond with younger brother
articles.body: Last year, Jason Kelce offered a rare look at how fame, family and the success of the “New Heights” podcast have reshaped his bond with younger brother Travis Kelce. The former Philadelphia Eagles centre explained that while the brothers have always been close, their relationship has matured as both built lives beyond football. Now, they speak more often, work together and remain closely connected with their families. Jason’s comments also showed how their roles have changed over time, with the brothers no longer simply sharing an older-younger sibling dynamic. Instead, he described Travis as his closest friend, highlighting a bond that has grown alongside their rise as two of football’s most recognisable brothers.Jason Kelce opens up about his relationship with Travis KelceJason Kelce and Travis Kelce spent years building their own NFL careers before becoming an even more prominent duo through their podcast. Jason spent his entire career with the Philadelphia Eagles, while Travis established himself as a key figure for the Kansas City Chiefs.Their shared work on “New Heights” has given the brothers another reason to stay in regular contact. Jason explained that the podcast has changed the way they interact, turning their sibling relationship into something that feels more like a friendship between equals.“Travis and I have been close for a long time,” he said as both brothers participated in the American Century Golf Championship.The former Eagles star then explained how their relationship has evolved since childhood.“Now with the [New Heights] podcast, we talk to each other more than we ever have. We loved each other growing up. We still love each other. Now it’s more like peer-to-peer, whereas growing up, being the older brother, it was a little bit different. Now it’s just, he’s my best friend on the planet. We get to talk once a week, and our families are close. He’s a great uncle.”Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce's bond beyond footballThe brothers' connection has continued to grow even as their careers have moved in different directions. Jason retired after a decorated Eagles career, while Travis remained with the Chiefs and continued chasing another Super Bowl.Their growing media presence has also brought them closer to a much wider audience. “New Heights” has become an important part of their public identity, but Jason’s comments suggest that the relationship behind the microphone remains deeply personal.Despite the attention surrounding Travis, including his high-profile relationship with Taylor Swift, Jason made it clear that their family connection remains at the heart of their bond. Their football careers helped make them famous, but their friendship as brothers has continued to shape their lives away from the field.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Softest middle finger to Gisele": Tom Brady’s Instagram post was allegedly a brutal message to Gisele Bündchen after welcoming baby with Joaquim Valente
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s relationship with Gisele Bündchen is back in the spotlight after a new biography made a striking claim about an Instagram post he shared
articles.body: Tom Brady’s relationship with Gisele Bündchen is back in the spotlight after a new biography made a striking claim about an Instagram post he shared shortly after Bündchen welcomed her first child with Joaquim Valente. The book suggests Brady’s football-themed caption carried a deeper message linked to tensions that had surrounded the couple’s marriage. The interpretation comes from people familiar with Brady’s life, rather than from Brady himself, adding another layer to the story of one of celebrity sports’ most closely followed divorces.Tom Brady’s post raises questions about Gisele BündchenAccording to Lars Anderson’s upcoming biography Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, Brady posted a photograph of himself throwing a football roughly a month after Bündchen gave birth in February 2025.The image might have appeared harmless on its own. However, the book argues that its timing and caption carried significance because football had reportedly been a major source of conflict during Brady and Bündchen’s marriage.The biography describes the post in detail:“Just over a month after the birth, Brady shared a photo of himself on Instagram — his preferred form of mass (and often cryptic) communication,” an excerpt from Brady published in the Daily Mail reads. “In the color photograph, Brady’s right arm is extended and a ball has spiraled out of his hand, silhouetted by the sunset’s golden glow. Underneath, Brady wrote: ‘True Love.’”The book then attributes an interpretation of the post to someone in Brady’s circle.“To those who knew him well, there was no ambiguity,” the book said of the Instagram post. “As one friend described it, that was ‘the softest middle finger.’”That description is an allegation contained in the biography, not a statement from Brady confirming that interpretation.What the new Tom Brady book claims about the divorceBrady and Bündchen ended their 13-year marriage in October 2022. They share two children, Benjamin and Vivian, while Brady also has a son, Jack, from his previous relationship with Bridget Moynahan.The new biography revisits the tensions that reportedly existed before their split, particularly disagreements over Brady’s decision to continue playing football.The book also presents another account of the breakup, claiming Bündchen’s interest in astrology influenced her decision. A source described as close to Brady told Anderson that she eventually concluded the pair were incompatible.Representatives for Brady and Bündchen were contacted for comment, according to Entertainment Weekly. Neither the Instagram caption nor the book’s interpretation establishes Brady’s intent as fact.Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness is scheduled for release on September 29, bringing renewed attention to the personal story behind Brady’s life after football and his highly publicised marriage to Bündchen.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brittany Mahomes shares what happened with Golden during Patrick Mahomes' Chiefs game
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes turned a Kansas City Chiefs game into a family outing as she brought her youngest daughter, Golden, to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes turned a Kansas City Chiefs game into a family outing as she brought her youngest daughter, Golden, to Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. While Patrick Mahomes led Kansas City to a 24-10 win over the Miami Dolphins, Brittany captured a tender moment between mother and daughter in the stands. The snapshot offered a quieter glimpse of the Mahomes family amid the excitement of an NFL game. Golden, dressed in Chiefs colours and sporting her dad’s famous No. 15, appeared ready to support her father before the stadium noise became too much.Brittany Mahomes shares sweet moment with GoldenBrittany shared the adorable moment on her Instagram Stories after arriving at the Miami stadium with Golden. In the photo, the toddler watched the action from the stands while Brittany gently covered her ears.The little girl wore a checked red-and-gold dress featuring “Mahomes 15,” a clear nod to her father and his role as the Chiefs’ quarterback. Brittany simply captioned the picture, “My Baby.”The family appearance came as Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs continued their 2026 campaign on the road. Kansas City controlled the game against Miami and finished with a 24-10 victory.Brittany also gave fans a glimpse of the strong Chiefs support inside Hard Rock Stadium. Sharing a view of the crowd, she wrote, “Man, so I love seeing Chiefs Kingdom show up always,” alongside a fire emoji.Patrick Mahomes celebrates another family milestoneThe game came shortly after Patrick celebrated his 31st birthday. Brittany marked the occasion with a heartfelt tribute that highlighted the quarterback’s role at home, away from the pressure of NFL Sundays.“Happy Birthday Babe!! You mean the world to us🥹🫶🏼 hope you feel so special and loved today but truly every day you’re so special to us!” Brittany wrote. “The heart of our family, we love you the MOST!❤️.”She also shared family photos featuring Patrick with their three children, Sterling Skye, Bronze and Golden.Patrick’s birthday celebrations also included close friends and Chiefs connections. He and Brittany were joined by Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift at 1587 Prime, the Kansas City steakhouse launched by Mahomes and Kelce in partnership with Noble 33.For the Mahomes family, Sunday’s game offered another chance to mix football with family time. Patrick handled the action on the field, while Brittany and Golden added a sweet moment from the stands that gave fans a glimpse of their life away from the spotlight.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ owners, the Hunt Family, have remained pretty passionate about the team as they focus on supporting them in the new season.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs’ owners, the Hunt Family, have remained pretty passionate about the team as they focus on supporting them in the new season. As the team remains unbeatable on the field in the new season, it seems the Hunt family is now looking into a billion dollar expansion project.Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire owners work on a billion dollar transformation project in the middle of the new seasonAs per report, the Kansas City Chiefs CEO and Chairman, Clark Hunt along with his brother Dan Hunt are working on developing the area surrounding FC Dallas's Toyota Stadium.There are plans to set up restaurants, a mini soccer pitch, a nine-story hotel with nearly 300 rooms and 40,000 square feet of convention space and about one million square feet of "premium office space."The billion dollar project is being worked on by the Hunt’s family’s Hunt Sports Development, along with Peak Curated Development and Venu Holding Corporation.As per NBC, the Kansas City Chiefs CEO and Chairman, Clark Hunt reflected on the family’s vision as he said, “Nearly three decades ago, my dad, Lamar Hunt, worked with the City of Frisco to build a stadium surrounded largely by farmland. He had a vision that someday it would become the center of a vibrant community…Today, it is our honor to build upon our dad’s legacy and help bring that vision to life.”FC Dallas President Dan Hunt said, "We hope our fans now, instead of spending two hours here or spending five or six hours, maybe a whole day here, enjoying the districts around the stadium and also then coming to the match that night…”Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire CEO Clark Hunt stands strong with the team through all the challenging daysFor now, the focus remains on the Kansas City Chiefs as the team has witnessed a winning streak in the new season after missing out on the playoffs in the last season.The Kansas City Chiefs CEO and Chairman, Clark Hunt has remained supportive of the team and had even supported quarterback Patrick Mahomes when he was getting trolled.A few months ago, the Kansas City Chiefs CEO and Chairman, Clark Hunt said in an interview,"I was with Patrick a couple of days ago in our training room, watching him go through the work he's doing to get back on the field. Nobody works harder than Patrick.”The billionaire owner added, "He certainly has a goal to be back for the beginning of the season,"At this point in time, all eyes remain on the Kansas City Chiefs clash in Week 4 after the team witnessed a winning streak against the Miami Dolphins, the Indianapolis Colts and the Denver Broncos.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Colin Simmons, jugador del equipo de fútbol americano de Texas, fue penalizado por conducta antideportiva por su gesto "vulgar" de "simular el uso del baño" durante una celebración ante Tennessee en la NCAA en la que simuló orinarse sobre el campo. Los comentaristas de ESPN no ocultaron su desagrado ante la celebración de Simons tras placar al quarterback Faizon Brandon (Tennessee). Fue una jugada defensiva de gran calibre por parte de Simmons, con Texas ganando 10-3 y restando unos cinco minutos para el final de la primera mitad,, pero fue lo que hizo después lo que provocó las críticas y los reproches de los comentaristas Kirk Herbstreit y Chris Fowler. "Es una estupidez, y difícilmente podría ser más vulgar", dijo Fowler. El 15 de marzo de 1997 Leandro, delantero del Valencia, se fue al córner del Estadio Vicente Calderón y simuló que orinaba como un perro sobre el banderín.

The Las Vegas Raiders had little business hiring one of the hottest head coaching candidates on the market this past offseason. They were an aimless, unserious franchise that hadn't won a division title since 2002.

But Klint Kubiak, coming off helping the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl title as their offensive coordinator, saw the potential when few did.

"There's just a lot to love about this organization," Kubiak said at his introductory media conference in February, via the team's site . "You look around this building and the resources that we have, our meal room, the weight room, the fields outside, the coaches offices, it's as good as it gets in the NFL. Been in a lot of buildings for good reasons and bad reasons, been hired and fired, and the resources are here. We've just got to go put it all together."

In three games, Kubiak has changed the Raiders. Last season was an absolute mess. The team went 3-14 and barely looked like a professional franchise. That wasn't unusual for the Raiders because they had been a mess for years.

Everything looks different this season. Las Vegas made good, smart decisions in free agency. The Maxx Crosby trade famously didn't work out but that is helping the Raiders this season. They had a plan for top draft pick Fernando Mendoza, to sit him and let Kirk Cousins play. The Raiders look like a competent team on both sides of the ball, with a front office making sharp decisions. It has been decades since that was the case.

The Raiders started 2-0 and it was fine to be skeptical, but a 35-27 win at the Saints might be a turning point . The Raiders forced a turnover on all four Saints possessions in the fourth quarter as they came back to win. The 2025 Raiders probably don't win that game. Neither would the 2024 Raiders, 2023 Raiders, 2022 Raiders or most Raiders teams since the Jon Gruden days, when they won their last playoff game.

Las Vegas' defense is second in the NFL in EPA allowed per play, a stunning turnaround from last season. The offense is 16th in EPA per play but two of those games came without Brock Bowers , who reminded everyone Sunday, with 116 yards and a touchdown, that he's the NFL's best tight end. Cousins is running a clean operation and the Kubiak influence on the offense is evident.

This weekend might be the biggest game for the Raiders since they moved to Las Vegas, though the team has been there only since 2020. They host the 3-0 Chiefs on Sunday afternoon. The Raiders have won two of their last five games against the Chiefs (one came against Chris Oladokun at QB, not Patrick Mahomes ), but this matchup is different. There's real hope for the Raiders coming into this meeting, not just a fleeting moment that gets washed away with another long losing streak. The Raiders will go into that game feeling confident they can win.

The Raiders are 3-0. And there are no signs yet that it's a mirage.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 3 of the NFL season:

The 1976 Buccaneers are the standard for bad teams in NFL history. They went 0-14 with -287 point differential, which is an NFL record. That's -20.5 per game. The 2026 Dolphins are 0-3 with a point differential of -50, which is -16.7 per game. The Dolphins aren't quite on the '76 Bucs' pace, but they're also not an expansion team.

And now Miami will be without running back De'Von Achane , the most talented player on the roster who suffered a season-ending torn ACL in Week 3. And still, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley is being optimistic. Miami lost by 14 points on Sunday to the Chiefs, but it was a one-score game until the final three minutes.

"That's why this one hurts," Hafley said, via Local10.com. "It's a four-point game in the third quarter. It's a seven-point game with us driving after we got backed up. We got the penalty to get the ball to the 50. I mean, I felt like we were right there."

Cam Ward 's final pass on Sunday was dispiriting. The Giants didn't score a touchdown, so Tennessee's defense did its job. Finally, in the fourth quarter, the Titans' offense woke up and had the ball inside the 10-yard line with a chance to take a lead in the final minute. And on first down, with two timeouts left, Ward had room to run but instead forced a pass that went right to safety Jevon Holland for an interception. Game over.

"He's out in the open, I'd just be smarter with the football," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said . "We've got two timeouts left, it's first-and-goal at the 8, we're going to score, you don't have to force it in that situation. Unfortunately it happened."

Saleh sounded exacerbated. Saleh was asked if Ward would be benched and he said no, but it has to be a consideration if Ward doesn't improve. Ward is 30th among 34 qualified quarterbacks in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play. Last season, he was 52nd of 60. There hasn't been any tangible progress.

The Buccaneers had to know they were taking a risk in going into the season with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels as their backup quarterback . Now Daniels is next in line with Baker Mayfield reportedly out two-to-four weeks with a thumb injury. The Buccaneers have Easton Stick on the practice squad, and at least he has four career starts. The Chargers , however, lost all four of those starts.

The Buccaneers are 2-10 in their last 12 games. They have not covered the point spread in 12 straight games, a record in the Super Bowl era . And now an 0-3 team has to somehow maintain with either an undrafted rookie or a practice squad journeyman at quarterback for maybe a month. Head coach Todd Bowles has to be the favorite to be the first head coach fired .

"Funny thing, we're 0-3 and we're a game out of first place," Bowles told the media after Sunday's game, via Pewter Report . "We have to get our stuff together. We got to reach down and do more. To a coach, to a person, or to a player, we've got to do more."

The Chargers' season has been fascinating. Last week, they matched the 1926 Racine Tornadoes by losing their first two games at home by double digits against teams that had a win percentage of less than .200 the previous season. On Sunday, they forced five turnovers, had a +4 turnover margin and still lost to the Bills. Teams posting those turnover numbers have lost only three times since 2013 and, amazingly, all three times the Chargers have been the losing team, according to Evan Abrams of Action Network.

The Chargers had more than enough breaks to beat the Bills and still somehow trailed 24-13 at the two-minute warning. Even if the Chargers don't feel like the fourth-worst team in the NFL, the results say they are.

At least the Cardinals woke up and realized they should be featuring Jeremiyah Love, the third overall pick of the draft. They gave him 21 of 23 running back carries and he had 90 yards. He added five receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown.

"Left a lot out there, I feel like," Love told ESPN . "I feel like I could help the team a lot more."

The Cardinals didn't play poorly against the 49ers , cutting their deficit to one score three different times in the fourth quarter. With that and a win at the Chargers already, the Cardinals might be a tougher out than expected.

The Jets were practically forced to give rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq (39% of offensive snaps through two games) a bigger role due to injuries to tight end Mason Taylor and receiver Adonai Mitchell . And Sadiq had a big breakout. He had seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown. The TD was a fantastic catch in the end zone.

"When you hear the play called in the huddle you know it's got a chance to go to you and then it comes out and you have a man-to-man look," Sadiq said, according to the team's site . "I know Geno [Smith] saw it and I saw it and it's just about going and making a play when your number is called."

The Jets are 1-2 but have been competitive all three weeks. They led in the fourth quarter against the Packers and were tied at Detroit on Sunday, though they lost both games. Developing young players is the main focus of this season. And Sadiq, an athletic freak who was the 16th overall pick, had a very promising showing on Sunday. That's a good sign.

The Panthers have a win over the Falcons when Atlanta was incompetent at quarterback. In their other two games they allowed 59 points to the Bears at home and on Sunday they lost to Deshaun Watson and the Browns .

Bryce Young leads the NFL with 939 passing yards, as he's on pace for more than 5,000. And the win over the Falcons was by 31 points. Maybe that's why the Panthers' start seems better than it actually has been. In reality, Carolina might be 0-3 if they faced a team with a decent quarterback in Week 2. The Panthers could argue that they would be 2-1 if a questionable roughing the passer call on Sunday against linebacker Bobby Okereke didn't wipe out an interception in the last two minutes, but overall the Panthers didn't play well enough to win.

"That's what it comes down to: a couple of red zone and fringe opportunities, came away with field goals and not touchdowns, big difference there," Panthers head coach Dave Canales said, via the team's site . "Missed a few turnover opps early on on the defensive side and gave them an opportunity to continue their drives, some untimely penalties, some things that really hurt us, and we've got to be smarter in some of those areas."

This is as low as the Packers have been ranked in a while. They haven't had a double-digit loss season since 2008. The Packers might not reach 10 losses this season either, but it has been an ugly start.

The defense was OK before it allowed 498 yards on Thursday to the Falcons' Michael Penix Jr., who hadn't played a game in 10 months. Green Bay 's offense is 25th in EPA per play and 30th in success rate, primarily because the offensive line is a mess. Jordan Love has been pressured on 44.4% of his dropbacks, according to PFF , which is a career high. The line isn't doing great blocking for a mediocre group of running backs either. The Packers average a league-worst 3 yards per carry. Head coach Matt LaFleur is on an early hot seat after that awful loss to the Falcons, in part because it's hard to figure out how the Packers turn it around.

"We've got to continue to work with these guys and try to figure out what we do well, because right now I don't know what we're doing well offensively," LaFleur said, via the team's site .

The Texans were 0-3 last season and went 12-5. So Houston can turn this around. But only six teams in NFL history, not counting the 1982 strike season, have made the playoffs after an 0-3 start, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press .

"0-3 is where we are right now," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire . "The only way we can do anything about it is to go through it. We're going through it right now, it's adversity, it happens. For me, it starts with me. I have to do a better job of getting our guys ready to roll."

The offense has been a problem. It has failed without Nico Collins , who has missed two games with a hamstring injury. Against a Colts defense that had allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two weeks, the Texans had 93 yards through three quarters. And 68 of those yards, and seven of their eight first downs, came on one drive. Even with Collins out, it shouldn't have been that hard to sustain drives. QB C.J. Stroud is looking for a contract extension , and the start to this season shouldn't be providing the Texans any optimism that he's worth the massive raise he's seeking.

When the Falcons play with a viable quarterback, they're 1-0 with a dominant road win at Green Bay. Maybe that's how we should judge the Falcons now. The 0-2 start with Cooper Rush mostly doesn't matter because now Atlanta is tied for first place in what again looks to be a putrid NFC South.

Michael Penix Jr. hasn't been a great quarterback yet but he looked phenomenal compared to the Falcons' other QBs. And Penix wouldn't be the first quarterback to break out in his third season. He was 18 of 25 for 256 yards against a Packers defense that had been decent through two weeks, and he provides hope for the offense moving forward.

"He felt comfortable, and that's how he looked," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said, via the team's site . "He looked comfortable in his game and he was balling."

Drake Maye 's struggles are now alarming . He leads the NFL with six interceptions and has a lost fumble, too. He's 28th in adjusted EPA per play after leading the league in that category last season. There aren't many instances of a quarterback who nearly won MVP in his second season falling this far in his third season, without some major injury involved.

On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel was asked if he believed Maye was dealing with any lingering effects of a shoulder injury. Vrabel said he wasn't aware of any physical setbacks for his QB. "I think when you go through an NFL game like that, especially as a quarterback, and you get hit, and again, there was not, to my knowledge, anything that would have put him on the injury report or any sort of treatment, " Vrabel said. " … I don't anticipate that being any issue going forward."

The Patriots on the whole look bad. They lost 35-6 to the Jaguars and now just have a narrow home win against the Steelers carrying their résumé.

It's not like the Commanders dominated on Sunday. They were outgained 437-258. They allowed 31 points at home. Marcus Mariota threw for just 183 yards and the Commanders averaged 2.6 yards per rush. That doesn't matter because the Commanders took advantage of all their opportunities to win 33-31, a victory that gives them hope of digging out of an 0-2 hole to start the season.

Also, Jayden Daniels could be close to a return. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told Albert Breer of The MMQB that Daniels is "more likely than not" to travel to London for the team's Week 4 game against the Colts, which gives him a shot to play two weeks after dislocating his left elbow.

The Browns have two close wins against the Buccaneers and Panthers, who are a combined 1-5 this season with the only win between them coming against a Cooper Rush-led Falcons team. Cleveland was outgained 360-259 by the Panthers at home on Sunday and caught a nice break that Deshaun Watson's late interception was nullified due to a questionable roughing the passer penalty. If you want to buy the Browns' 2-1 start that's fine, but there are not a lot of signs that this is sustainable going forward.

If there is an argument to be made that the Browns can keep this going, it's their defense. After a horrific Week 1 against the Jaguars, the defense has been sixth in the NFL in EPA allowed per play over the last two weeks. Mike Rutenberg took over defensive coordinator job from Jim Schwartz this past offseason and the opening game was concerning, but the group has settled in since then.

The best news for the Colts is that Daniel Jones continues to make progress. A slow start should have been expected as he was returning from a torn Achilles, and he looked rusty at times in the first two games. In Week 3, against a very good Texans defense, Jones completed 24 of 36 passes for 235 yards. He came up with enough plays on the final drive to get Indianapolis in position for a game-winning field goal, after it looked like the Colts might blow a 16-7 lead in the fourth quarter and fall to 0-3. Jones fumbled three times, losing two, but facing defensive end Will Anderson Jr. is tough for any quarterback.

Overall, Jones is progressing. Don't forget how good he was for the first half of last season before the injury.

"Can't turn the ball over like that, costly for the team," Jones said . "Can't put the team in that position and certainly understand how important that is as a quarterback, but the game goes on and you've got to be able to play the next play and execute."

The Saints led the Raiders 27-16 in the second half and it looked like they were on their way to an impressive 2-1 start to the season. But their four fourth-quarter possessions ended with: fumble, interception, fumble, fumble. It's the second time in Saints history they've had four turnovers in a quarter, with the other instance coming in the third quarter of a 1990 game against the Lions, according to Jeff Duncan of the New Orleans Times- Picayune . It was a historic meltdown.

But overall there were some positives. Tyler Shough again looked good with four touchdown passes. Chris Olave had 107 receiving yards. Chase Young had two more sacks. The Saints' 1-2 record belies that they've played good football, and are a failed 2-point conversion at Detroit and a horrible fourth quarter vs. the Raiders from being much higher on this list.

"I think, in many ways, there is a lot of good stuff on this film," Saints head coach Kellen Moore said, according to transcripts . "As painful as this loss is, as frustrating as this loss is, we can't let this thing linger too long. We were in a position to finish that game, and we didn't finish it. We had our opportunities and were not able to get it done. We have to recognize the entire film, not just the ending."

Maybe the Steelers stumbled upon a solution for their offense: Turn Jaylen Warren into a workhorse. Last season, he played 47.4% of the Steelers' snaps, a lower percentage than Kenneth Gainwell . In Week 1, with Rico Dowdle having been added over the offseason, Warren was at 37.3% of snaps. Dowdle was injured in Week 2, and in Week 3 Warren had the backfield to himself. He had 127 rushing yards on 17 carries and 49 receiving yards on three catches. That opened up the Steelers' offense, which hadn't played that well through two weeks. Aaron Rodgers had a strong game with 292 yards and three touchdowns.

Dowdle is considered day to day, but the Steelers have to consider giving Warren a much larger role after what he showed in Week 3.

"Jaylen Warren was dynamic, absolutely dynamic, and guys made some plays down the field," Rodgers said, via the team's site . "Had some explosion in the offense back, especially in the run game."

One image sums up the Cowboys ' loss to the Ravens :

How? The Cowboys completely blew the final 23 seconds. They threw it incomplete on first down, then took a false start before second down. On third down, Dak Prescott, despite plenty of time and no pressure, threw it away instead of waiting for George Pickens, who was wide open. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Prescott was throwing it away, for some reason, and took the blame by saying he had been stressing to make sure Dallas didn't blow the field goal opportunity.

"That's on me," Schottenheimer said . "I over-coached him."

After taking the tying field goal, the Cowboys kicked off for a touchback, leaving seven seconds on the clock. That's a bad clock management error because it gave the Ravens enough time to get a completion and a long field goal. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter admitted his team might have decided to go to overtime if there was any less time on the clock.

"Honestly, anything less than seven seconds, it would have been really hard to do the play that we did," Minter said, according to the transcripts. "We may have even just ran the clock out. But [with] seven seconds left, and with the touchback rules, they decided to kick a touchback [and] gave us the ball on the 35. We really only needed 18-plus yards to get to our end-of-game type of range."

The Cowboys might still be good this season, but that loss will linger.

We saw the Giants' limitations on offense Sunday without Jaxson Dart. Against a Tennessee defense that's average at best, New York couldn't score a touchdown. It had 238 yards, with just 118 from Jameis Winston and the passing game. It was a rainy day in New Jersey but it's still unlikely we see much more from the offense going forward.

The Giants made a low-cost trade for J.J. McCarthy on Monday, sending a fifth-round pick to the Vikings for a player who was the 10th pick of the draft just two years ago. It's hard to buy that McCarthy, who has struggled in the NFL, could join the Giants midseason and be the answer. It's more of a developmental trade, and providing depth for later in the season if Winston doesn't turn it around. It's just hard to expect too much, whether it's Winston or McCarthy at quarterback.

The Eagles' 2-0 start was shaky. They barely squeezed out wins over the Commanders and Titans. Philadelphia might have been exposed on Monday night. Its offense was dreadful, barely scoring seven points. Jalen Hurts was poor, and was completely outplayed by Bears 38-year-old third-stringer Case Keenum. Hurts did not look comfortable, and hasn't in the Eagles' new scheme for much of the season. The defense, which had been good but not great during the 2-0 start, was shredded by the aforementioned Keenum, who hadn't taken an NFL regular-season snap since 2023. The Eagles will probably be a good team. They're also pretty close to being 0-3 to start this season. There is a lot that needs to be fixed for the Eagles to get anywhere near an elite level.

The Lions have given up the most points and second-most yards in the NFL this season. They beat the Jets on Sunday but allowed 335 yards and 24 points. Two Jets, Garrett WIlson and Kenyon Sadiq, had 100-yard receiving games. Most Lions games this season will be high scoring. They'll need the defense to make a few plays, like it did in the final minute. The Jets reached the Lions' 28-yard line, but safety Chuck Clark sacked Geno Smith on a blitz, causing a fumble that the Lions recovered.

"And then for our defense to have to, man, they had to make that stop," Lions head coach Campbell said . "That's what it was going to come down to. And it was such a great call by [defensive coordinator] Kelvin Sheppard and those guys executing it."

So much for that notion that the Bengals ' defense is much improved. The Steelers' offense, which ranked 31st in EPA per play through two weeks, had 411 yards and 30 points. The Steelers had only one offensive touchdown through two weeks.

This was a typical Bengals game through the past few years, in which the offense plays well enough to win and the defense isn't good enough. It looked fixed through two weeks, especially in a 20-6 win over Houston. Now all of the old concerns have reemerged. Special teams didn't help either, with a roughing the punter penalty that led to a Steelers touchdown and a muffed punt that gave Pittsburgh three more points.

"Some games you just go get your butt kicked and there's not much to say about it," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said, according to transcripts . "This one, we had our chances. Pittsburgh took advantage of theirs. We didn't take advantage of ours."

Case Keenum will be the feel-good story from the Bears' impressive win over the Eagles on Monday night, and rightfully so. A 38-year-old third-string quarterback played a great game. But the Bears' defense might be much better than expected. In Week 2, they gave up nine points to the Vikings, but that was mostly dismissed because Chicago lost that game. On Monday night the Bears allowed seven points, and had the Eagles' snap on the final play of the first half been a half-second later, it would have been a shutout. If the Bears' defense is even above average, the offense will be very good when Caleb Williams returns, or apparently no matter who is playing quarterback.

Don't forget that the Raiders are winning despite zero snaps from the first overall pick of the NFL Draft, while most other teams are getting immediate contributions from their top-drafted rookie. The plan to have Fernando Mendoza sit and learn hasn't hurt the on-field product yet. The hot start probably means it will be a while before Mendoza plays. It seemed like Mendoza could take over sometime near the midpoint of the season , but it would probably take an immediate losing streak (or an injury to Kirk Cousins, of course) to happen anytime in October.

Mendoza might be sitting for a long time, and the idea that he could sit the whole season is in play. For the 3-0 Raiders, that's for all the right reasons.

The Vikings' offense was bad on Sunday. Starting with the team's second drive of the game, Minnesota had a 10-possession stretch in which it had eight punts, one interception and one touchdown. Kyler Murray was in his first full game in a new system, and he played most of the game without superstar Justin Jefferson after Jefferson left with an ankle injury. Murray had just 168 yards on 29 attempts and had the worst success rate of any quarterback through Sunday's games in Week 3. He was at 21.6%, and the second-worst mark was 28.3%.

It was a poor performance by Murray and the offense but it was also another win.

"It wasn't perfect by any means," Murray said, according to the team's site . "But at the end of the day we're 3-0."

The Broncos got their second straight win against a quality opponent, but there are things to clean up. The Rams had 482 yards to 257 for the Broncos. Denver's offense was awful in the first half, which has been the case in four of the six halves the Broncos have played this season. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb seemed like he might be close to losing play-calling to Sean Payton before the offense started moving in the third quarter. The Broncos made the plays they had to in order to win and deserve credit for that, but a team that has been outgained by 317 yards and outscored by 10 points this season needs to play better, especially in the first half.

"I'm comfortable with the grit of a team that can play well in the fourth quarter," Broncos coach Sean Payton said, according to transcripts. "I'm uncomfortable with how we play at the start of games, if that's a fair answer."

You can't simply dismiss a bad half, because those count too. But if we take out the second half of Jacksonville's Week 2 game against the Broncos — many teams wear down in the second half at Denver's altitude, particularly early in the season — the Jaguars have outscored their three opponents 79-19. Had Jacksonville played a little better against the Broncos in the second half, perhaps their dominant start would be getting more attention. Maybe the Patriots will prove to be a bad team, but they were 14-3 last season and won the AFC, and Jacksonville beat them 35-6 on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence has a 107.8 passer rating this season, and his career high over a full season is 95.2. There are many things to like about the Jaguars' start.

The Jaguars have some tough games coming up (at Bengals, vs. Eagles in London, vs. Texans in London, vs. Colts, at Ravens) but keep your mind open to the Jaguars being one of the NFL's best teams this season.

Dropping the Rams even this far doesn't seem like it will age well. The Rams played on Sunday night at Denver, a team that is 16-4 in its last 20 games, and lost in the final minute after a bad defensive pass interference call . They were without two players who are arguably top 10 non-quarterbacks in the NFL, Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua. It was a reasonable loss. Check the Super Bowl betting odds: The Rams are still favorites at some books, or just behind the Bills. They're 1-2 but don't be fooled into thinking this isn't a very good team. The Rams will be just fine.

Still, 1-2 isn't how the Rams wanted to start . Even if the pass interference call was bad, the Rams were sloppy when it mattered.

The Rams have some things to clean up, and if Nacua and Garrett are out a while it will be a challenge, like it would be for any team losing two players at that level. But listen to the oddsmakers. The Rams will still be a Super Bowl contender.

The Ravens' win over the Cowboys wasn't just dramatic, it was one of a kind. The Ravens' game-winning drive started with seven seconds left, which is the latest a game-winning drive has started after a kickoff since 1978, according to ESPN Insights . It was also the first time in the Super Bowl era that each team made a field goal in the last 10 seconds of regulation, ESPN Insights said.

Lamar Jackson had, not one, but two clutch drives. He took the team 64 yards to score a go-ahead touchdown with 1:30 left and after Baltimore's defense let Dallas tie it, then Jackson hit Zay Flowers on the crucial 27-yard gain that set up the game-winning field goal. He also kept his cool and knew to get a timeout with one second left. The Ravens have blown some games in the fourth quarter the past few years, including one to the Saints in Week 2, but winning like they did Sunday could carry over for a while.

The Chiefs are 3-0 but if there's a concern, it's still the passing offense around Patrick Mahomes. In particular, Xavier Worthy has been surprisingly quiet. In three games, he has 18, 25 and 20 yards. Miami has a poor secondary and Worthy managed only two catches for 20 yards. The hope that the 2024 first-round draft pick could break out in his third season is dwindling.

Other than that, the Chiefs are doing well. The worry is what happens if Kenneth Walker, who is carrying the offense, wears down under the biggest workload of his career or misses time. There's not much else around him for Mahomes to work with.

The Seahawks aren't dropping too far after a loss because it seems unlikely they'll allow 33 points again soon. Seattle allowed only 258 yards, and one of the scores was a pick 6, so the defense will be fine. Sam Darnold should be fine too. He returned from an injury and had four touchdowns, though his two interceptions were a problem.

One troubling aspect is Jadarian Price's start to the season. The rookie first-round draft pick fumbled Sunday and was effectively benched, getting only two more carries after the turnover. He finished with five carries for 15 yards. He has lost a fumble in two straight weeks. The Seahawks can speak positively about the rookie but their actions show they don't fully trust him.

"I think it's as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said . "I know he didn't come back after the initial fumble; we just decided to calm it down and bring him back after the half. But he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out; he'll be fine."

The 49ers move up but the injuries are alarming. They lost defensive end Nick Bosa in practice during the week and then receiver Mike Evans and offensive tackle Trent Williams during the game, though it sounds like neither one of those injuries is serious . The 49ers won't get to play the Dolphins and Cardinals every week.

Or maybe everything will be just fine if Brock Purdy avoids the 49ers' weird injury bug. Purdy is playing excellent football, leading the NFL with nine touchdown passes and a sparkling 133.1 passer rating. It's a remarkable run he's on and the main reason the 49ers are 3-0 and second in the power rankings.

The Bills were very sloppy on Sunday. They lost three fumbles and Josh Allen threw two interceptions. Allen, who had been on a phenomenal tear through two games, had a 54 passer rating on Sunday. Not counting Allen's rookie season, he has had a lower passer rating only four times in his career. And despite playing far below average, the Bills were up by 11 points with two minutes left and won by eight.

Allen is unlikely to play that poorly very often this season, and the Bills as a team might not turn it over five times in a game the rest of the season. They didn't turn it over more than three times in game last regular season (they did turn it over five times against the Broncos in a divisional round loss) and hadn't turned it over five times since Week 7 of 2018, when Allen was a rookie. The Bills were at their worst, or very close to it, and still won, which is a good indicator that they're a dominant team.

articles.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts struggles as Philadelphia loses to Case Keenum-led Bears
articles.summary: The Eagles were blown out by the Bears on Monday night.
articles.body:
Case Keenum completely outplayed Jalen Hurts on Monday night. Let that sink in. It will in Philadelphia overnight.

Keenum, the Bears ' third-string quarterback who was pressed into duty, was a fun story on Monday night. He won't be the story in Philadelphia on Tuesday morning.

Being dominated 27-7 to a shorthanded Chicago Bears team will make for an interesting day on Philly sports talk radio, especially with how Hurts and the Eagles' offense failed repeatedly to move the ball. The Eagles had a shaky 2-0 start, and the loss to the Bears wasn't their finest moment. The offense that struggled belonged to the Eagles, not the team with a 38-year-old quarterback who hadn't taken an NFL snap since 2023.

Keenum did play well. He was 24 of 34 for 247 yards, a pair of touchdowns and no interceptions. He made a case to keep the starting job until injured starter Caleb Williams returns. Normal backup Tyson Bagent didn't play Monday night after being in concussion protocol most of last week.

"This Texas boy loves Chicago," the Texas-born Keenum told ESPN after the game. "This is a cool spot. We're going to celebrate this one tonight."

While Keenum was good, Hurts was not. He was 15 of 22 for just 140 yards by the time the Bears took a 20-point lead about midway through the fourth quarter. He padded his stats a bit after that but not much. Definitely not enough to match Keenum, who was appearing with his eighth NFL team on Monday night. Hurts finished 16 of 25 for 153 yards and a 64.2 passer rating. Keenum's rating was 110.8.

There will be plenty to talk about in Philly this week.

Eagles on wrong end of controversial sequence

The Eagles offense needed all the help it could get on Monday, and it missed out on a possible seven points due to Hurts being sent off to be evaluated for a concussion .

Hurts was hit late as he was going out of bounds by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson, which was flagged. He was then forced to leave the game to go to the blue medical tent to be checked for a concussion. While Hurts was being evaluated, Saquon Barkley had a run down to the 1-yard line. That's when the Eagles usually run the tush push, which is just about automatic. But with Hurts in the tent, Andy Dalton wasn't an option to run it.

Right before Hurts walked out of the tent, Dalton threw a terrible interception to rookie safety Dillon Thieneman in the end zone. When Hurts saw it he screamed in frustration, as the Eagles were denied a touchdown due to a concussion evaluation when Hurts didn't have one — after a hit that was clearly illegal by Chicago.

"Obviously frustrating," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni told ESPN at halftime. "The doctors have to do their job. They've got to protect these guys."

The Eagles offense, which could have used that touchdown, didn't score until a frenetic final play of the first half. The Eagles had to scramble when DeVonta Smith got stopped at the 1-yard line, barely getting the snap off with one second left and Hurts scoring on a quarterback sneak as time ran out in the half.

The Eagles trailed 10-7 at the half and had to feel like they should have led at halftime. It might not have mattered, because the Eagles offense never showed up in the second half. Had the snap at the end of the first half came about a half-second later, Philadelphia would have been shut out.

The Eagles got that clutch play right before halftime but couldn't build off it. The Bears came out as the better team in the third quarter.

Keenum found Kalif Raymond wide open in the middle of the Eagles' secondary and he ran for a 41-yard touchdown. That gave Chicago a 20-7 lead. While the Eagles offense was not good on Monday, the defense wasn't stellar, either.

The Eagles' first three possessions of the second half were all three-and-outs. On the fourth drive they went for it on a fourth down and Hurts threw a bad interception in which he seemed to not see linebacker T.J. Edwards underneath. That meant Hurts had as many interceptions in the third quarter as the Eagles had first downs.

Hurts — in a new scheme this season and with A.J. Brown off to New England — didn't play with much confidence. He didn't throw it accurately and rarely made anything happen downfield, with just one completion of 20 yards or more. He didn't look much like the quarterback who won Super Bowl MVP two seasons ago.

After the interception, Keenum snuck in for a touchdown, his first rushing touchdown this decade. That put the Bears, who lost 9-3 last week at home to the Vikings, ahead by 20 points.

The loss to the Bears reframes the Eagles' 2-0 start. They barely beat the Commanders at home, needing to stop a two-point conversion at the end. They barely beat a now 0-3 Titans team, needing a touchdown with nine seconds left to pull off a comeback win. Philadelphia isn't too far from being 0-3 to start the season.

There is always some angst in Philadelphia, even when the Eagles are winning. After Monday night, Eagles fans have something legitimate to complain about.

articles.title: Chicago Bears 27-7 Philadelphia Eagles: Case Keenum shines on first start since 2023
articles.summary: Veteran quarterback Case Keenum throws for two touchdowns and rushes for another as the Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFL.
articles.body:
Veteran quarterback Case Keenum starred on his first start for almost three years as the Chicago Bears handed the Philadelphia Eagles their first defeat of the season.

Starting his first NFL game since December 2023, the 38-year-old threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for another as the Bears won 27-7 at Soldier Field in Chicago.

It is the first time he has thrown multiple touchdowns in a game since October 2019, while he is also the oldest player to score a rushing touchdown for the Bears.

Keenum, an NFL journeyman playing at his eighth franchise, was called into action because of a knee injury to Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent's concussion.

Wide receiver Kalif Raymond, who scored a touchdown, said: "He was like, 'I may not be a cowboy, but this is definitely not my first rodeo - a lot of confidence in him; a lot of confidence in himself.

"He practises, preps every week, but particularly this week. We didn't expect anything different from him."

Keenum's first drive resulted in a touchdown for Luther Burden III, and Cairo Santos added a 29-yard field goal before Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts rushed for a touchdown to cut the Bears' half-time lead to 10-7.

Santos added a second field goal early in the third quarter before the Bears scored two touchdowns among 17 unanswered points.

The Bears defence limited the Eagles to 248 yards and picked off an interception off Jalen Hurts and replacement Andy Dalton.
